title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page sets up a combinatorial model of a map in the sense of Grothendieck's 'dessins/cartes', with the map not assumed oriented. It serves as the preparatory first page of a construction continued on the next page.

Setup:
- X is a combinatorial map, possibly non-orientable.
- R is its set of flags ('repères').
- S = S_0 ⊔ S_1 ⊔ S_∞ is the set of vertices, edges and faces ('feuilles'). Each is identified with its centre R_φ in the underlying topological surface 𝒳, so S ⊂ 𝒳.
- A flag r = (s, a, f) is identified with the triangle of the barycentric subdivision with vertices R_s, R_a, R_f, carrying indices 0, 1, ∞.
- Each such triangle is oriented by the cyclic order 0 → 1 → ∞ (the 'orientation of the flag'). Adjacent triangles therefore have opposite local orientations, which is why the figure carries ± signs.

Involutions: τ_i(r) is the flag adjacent to r across the side opposite the vertex of type i. So τ_0 changes the vertex, τ_1 the edge, τ_∞ the face.

Rotations defined from them:
- ρ_∞ = τ_1τ_0 (with ρ_∞^{-1} = τ_0τ_1) fixes the face. It is the one-step rotation about the ∞-vertex, in the sense given by r's orientation; the inverse goes the other way.
- ρ_0 = τ_∞τ_1 (with inverse τ_1τ_∞) is the rotation about the 0-vertex.
- ρ_1 = τ_0τ_∞ = τ_∞τ_0 is the half-turn about the edge midpoint. The two compositions agree because a non-degenerate edge has exactly four flags.

Recalled presentation of the cartographic group C_2:
- τ_0² = τ_1² = τ_∞² = (τ_0τ_∞)² = 1.
- ρ_∞ρ_1ρ_0 = 1, which follows by telescoping: τ_1τ_0·τ_0τ_∞·τ_∞τ_1 = 1.

The orientation-preserving words in the ρ's generate the index-2 subgroup, the oriented cartographic group ⟨ρ_0, ρ_1, ρ_∞ | ρ_1² = ρ_0ρ_1ρ_∞ = 1⟩ ≅ PSL_2(Z)-type quotient data.

Purpose: the next page introduces auxiliary points R_r^{i,j} near the corners of each flag-triangle and arcs λ_r^i, a_r^i around them, subject to identification relations. This builds an explicit cell or groupoid structure on 𝒳 \ S, or a thickening of it, compatible with the canonical conformal realisation. Presumably it is meant for computing fundamental groupoids and Galois/Teichmüller actions with tangential base points. The previous pages concern an elliptic (torus) example.
errors: The marginal phrase reads as 'rotation ... autour des sommets de type ∞ resp. 0'. Formula (1) gives both ρ_∞ and ρ_∞^{-1} about the face (type ∞) centre, so the 'resp.' must refer to direct versus inverse sense, not to type ∞ versus type 0. The rotation about type-0 vertices is introduced separately in (2). This is likely a transcription or wording ambiguity rather than a mathematical error.

The relation (τ_0τ_∞)² = 1 and the equality τ_0τ_∞ = τ_∞τ_0 implicitly assume that each edge has two distinct endpoints-sides, i.e. a standard map without free or half edges. This is fine under the usual conventions.

ideas.what: Flags of a (possibly non-orientable) map identified with triangles of the barycentric subdivision. Three involutions τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞ are defined by adjacency.
ideas.modern_name: Flag/monodromy description of maps; cartographic group C_2 = ⟨σ_0, σ_1, σ_2 | σ_i², (σ_0σ_2)²⟩
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984); Jones–Singerman (1978); Bryant–Singerman (1985) for non-orientable maps; also Tutte-style flag systems

ideas.what: Rotations ρ_0, ρ_1, ρ_∞ as products of adjacent involutions, with ρ_∞ρ_1ρ_0 = 1 and ρ_1² = 1.
ideas.modern_name: Oriented cartographic group C_2^+ (quotient of PSL_2(Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3 type data); dessin monodromy (σ_0, σ_1, σ_∞)

ideas.what: Preparation, completed on the next page, of a refined cell structure: corner points R_r^{i,j} and arcs around each flag-triangle. Intended to model 𝒳 minus S combinatorially, compatibly with the canonical conformal realisation.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial model of the fundamental groupoid with tangential base points on a dessin
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura, Drinfeld-type tangential base point techniques (1980s–90s)
ideas.where_published: Hinted at in Esquisse (Teichmüller tower, base points); no explicit published construction known

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard set-up of the flag/cartographic-group formalism, which Grothendieck himself published in the Esquisse and which Jones–Singerman and others developed. The more original groupoid/cell construction only starts on the next page.
transcription_corrections: Above line 2 the insertion is 'sommets arêtes faces' (glossing S_0, S_1, S_∞). The line reads roughly 'l'ens de ces feuilles, identifiées à leurs centres, dans [l'espace] topologique sous-jacent, désignons par 𝒳 ...'.
'opposés respectivement aux 2[?] sommets d'indice[?] type 0, 1, ∞' should read 'opposés respectivement aux sommets de type 0, 1, ∞ de r'.
'dans le sens inverse[?]' is plausible for the illegible word. Context implies ρ_∞^{-1} is the rotation in the opposite sense about the same face centre.
In (5), the final relation is ρ_∞ρ_1ρ_0 = 1, with a crossed-out ρ_∞ after it, as transcribed.
Figure labels: the triangle labelled with τ_∞(r) also bears ρ_1(r) = τ_0τ_∞(r) = τ_∞τ_0(r) in an adjacent region. The triangle labels ρ_∞^{-1}(r) = τ_0τ_1(r) and τ_∞τ_1(r) = ρ_0(r) are as stated.
